title: slotting-and-batch-taxonomy-weekly-notes
content:
Weekly standup notes: Slotting & batch taxonomy (informal capture)

Context and goal:
- Goal for this sprint: reduce tail latency variability introduced by aggressive micro-batching when high-slot churn occurs (hot-path is prefill + slot reallocation).
- New term: slotting = per-GPU logical assignment of active KV-context slots (not physical CUDA streams). We need clearer naming in code + dashboards.

This week's highlights:
1) Slotting prototype v2 landed on dev cluster (Marcus)
  - Ran canary across 8 machines (g5x2-equivalent), 72h soak.
  - Observed median token latency improvement ~5%, p95 reduced by ~12% for mixed-length chat workload (seq len distribution: 32% short, 50% med, 18% long).
  - Memory fragmentation edge-case: small increase in GPU memory tail events when slot compaction triggered (seen in 2/72h windows).

2) KV cache soft-eviction heuristic updated (Sofia)
  - Heuristic: prefer evicting slots with lowest reuse-score over LRU to preserve prefix-heavy workloads.
  - Offline sim (trace-replay) shows hit-rate maintained, evictions reduced in multi-session spike tests.
  - Still seeing a small regression for seq-heavy rerankers — follow-up: add per-route reuse weights.

3) Batch taxonomy refactor (Diego + Ellen)
  - Introduced explicit batch classes: interactive, background, prefill, rerank. Router will tag requests; kernel now applies different batching aggressiveness per class.
  - Integration tests added. Some routes fail if request tagging missing — added a fallback mapping to infer class from headers.

Operational notes / incidents:
- Mar 6 03:12 UTC: Canary host dm-8 produced repeated slot compaction spikes after 2h of 95% load. Root cause: race between compaction thread and kernel handoff; fix submitted as PR 872 (Marcus).
- Temporary mitigation: autoscale up by 1 slot per GPU for affected canary pools.

Numbers & quick metrics (canary vs baseline):
- baseline p95 token latency: 110ms; canary p95: 97ms (down 12%).
- median token latency: baseline 24ms -> canary 23ms (5% improvement overall).
- batch fill factor variance: baseline stdev 14% -> canary stdev 9% (smoother).
- KV cache hitrate: baseline 86% -> canary 85.5% (stat noise, see reranker regression).

Open questions / unknowns:
- How do we weigh reuse-score vs LRU across mixed workloads? Proposal: per-route policy with a global fallback. Need an easy UI knob in Console for trials. (RW-5728)
- Slot compaction race root cause fully identified, but need more reproducible test harness. Can we synthesize the 95% sustained load with precise churn patterns? (ACTION: Marcus + SRE)
- Will batch taxonomy increase cold-start latency for ephemeral API keys that never set headers? We have fallback but we should measure default behavior. (Diego)

Decisions made:
- Proceed with slotting v2 rollout to canary pool for the week after next if PR passes extended soak and the memory fragmentation spike is addressed.
- Ship batch taxonomy with conservative defaults (interactive -> low batching, prefill -> aggressive). Allow per-route overrides.

Action items (owner, due):
- Marcus: add deterministic compaction test harness and reproduce dm-8 behavior (due 2029-03-12).
- Sofia: implement per-route reuse-weight config and wire it to Optimize recommendations (RW-5812) (due 2029-03-19).
- Diego: run default-tag fallback load test against edge pool and report cold-start metrics (due 2029-03-13).
- Ellen: update Console rollout docs + add a one-click toggle for "slotting-experimental" in staging (due 2029-03-15).
- All: add 3 more routes to canary (low-traffic production) to diversify workload traces (due 2029-03-14).

Notes to self / half-baked thoughts:
- Might be worth naming slot bucket IDs with human-readable prefixes for debugging (e.g., slot-interactive-23) — makes logs easier.
- If per-route reuse weights are too noisy, think about autoscaling thresholds that consider reuse-weighted occupancy.
- Consider lightweight telemetry: expose slot churn per-minute metric to Console to detect noisy customers early.

Links / references used this week:
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/872 (slot compaction lock fix)
- Design doc: confluence.redwood.com/display/SERV/slotting-design-v2
- Incident notes: JIRA RW-5728 (compaction spikes)
- Feature request: JIRA RW-5812 (per-route reuse weight)

Meeting cadence / next meeting:
- Slotting sync: Tue 09:30 PST (weekly) — aim to shorten to 30m and focus on action updates only.
- Post-rollout retrospective: schedule once canary passes extended soak (tentative Mar 22).

Misc:
- Small housekeeping: rename telemetry metric slot_alloc/slot_free to slot.alloc and slot.free to align with Prom naming scheme. (Ellen)
- Team morale: positive — canary soak success is a small win.

End of notes.
plain_text_preview: Slotting & batch taxonomy weekly standup. Owner: Aditi Rao. Key leads: Marcus, Sofia, Diego, Ellen. Canary showed p95 down 12% but small mem fragmentation spike. Action items assigned; PR 872 fixed a race. Next: compaction harness, per-route reuse weights, expanded canary.
